text.p: These are the leading stories in the Botswana press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Botswana and South Africa are installing a low noise telephone link between their two countries to help ease the frequent congestion on the present analogue and digital microwave links, the Botswana Telecommunication Corporation said.

- The Southern African Development Community (SADC) has denied press reports from Namibia that it issued an ultimatum to its members who also belong to the Common Market for East and Southern Africa (COMESA) to resign from that organisation.

- An Anglican priest from Uganda, attached to the Botswana health ministry to advise on the role of the church in fighting AIDS, is being criticised for his outspoken ways which include lessons from the pulpit on the use of condoms.
